papers.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents routinely interact with untrusted external data, exposing them to indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks that hijack agents into executing attacker-chosen tasks. To uncover these vulnerabilities at scale, automated red-teaming methods often leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to generate attacks that achieve high attack success rates (ASR). Model developers use the attacks discovered during internal red-teaming to harden agents through adversarial training before deployment, a collaborative offensive-defensive process known in cybersecurity as purple-teaming. However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training. Specifically, we find that two state-of-the-art RL-based red-teaming methods, RL-Hammer and PISmith, suffer from mode collapse, repeatedly discovering similar attack strategies whose additional successes add no additional robustness improvements to adversarial training. To address this gap, we introduce PIPETTE, a unified prompt injection purple-teaming framework that effectively converts red-teaming discoveries into defender robustness improvements. PIPETTE employs a dictionary learning-based reward that encourages broader coverage of attack strategies during red-teaming. It also integrates an on-policy adversarial training pipeline tailored to IPI defense, enabling agents to resist attacks while completing legitimate user tasks. Extensive evaluations across agentic benchmarks (AgentDojo and ASB) demonstrate that PIPETTE produces defenders that achieve near-zero attack success rates on static attacks and can withstand strong adaptive attacks, while maintaining benign task utility close to that of the undefended baseline.

summary_es.tldr: PIPETTE mejora la seguridad de agentes LLM contra ataques de inyección de prompts mediante un enfoque de 'purple-teaming' más robusto.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes LLM son vulnerables a ataques de inyección de prompts indirectos (IPI) que secuestran sus funciones. Los métodos actuales de 'red-teaming' basados en RL descubren ataques repetitivos que no mejoran significativamente la robustez tras el entrenamiento adversarial.
summary_es.propuesta: PIPETTE es un marco de 'purple-teaming' que utiliza aprendizaje por diccionario para fomentar la diversidad de ataques durante el 'red-teaming' y un entrenamiento adversarial adaptado para la defensa contra IPI, manteniendo la utilidad de las tareas.
summary_es.resultados: Los agentes defendidos con PIPETTE logran tasas de éxito de ataque cercanas a cero contra ataques estáticos y resisten ataques adaptativos fuertes, manteniendo una utilidad de tarea similar a la de los agentes sin defensa.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Asegura que los agentes LLM sean más seguros y confiables en entornos del mundo real al abordar de manera efectiva las vulnerabilidades de inyección de prompts, protegiendo contra el secuestro de tareas.

papers.title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Prompt injection is the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents, and the community now agrees that robustness must be measured against adaptive attackers rather than fixed benchmark injections. Many adaptive red teamers exist, and most are built to maximize attack success rate (ASR). Yet ASR counts how often a target breaks, not in how many different ways. A red teamer can achieve a high ASR by reusing a few techniques that work, leaving the others untested and absent from the attacks used to harden models. We present AutoPI, an adaptive red teamer designed to find many different ways to break a target, not just to break it often. AutoPI uses PIAtlas, a taxonomy of prompt-injection techniques, both to guide its search and to measure coverage. For each scenario, an attacker LLM writes an injection for every sub-technique in the taxonomy and then reworks the ones that fail using feedback from an LLM judge. The method is black-box and training-free, it plugs into existing benchmarks in place of their fixed attack templates, and it stays up to date as the taxonomy evolves. We evaluate AutoPI on AgentDojo and IPI Arena against open-weight and proprietary target models. Alongside ASR, we report technique coverage, the fraction of taxonomy classes, techniques, and sub-techniques that yield at least one successful injection. On AgentDojo, AutoPI finds a successful injection against Qwen3.6-35B in all six classes of the taxonomy and for more than 90% of its techniques. Against Claude Haiku 5.5, the most robust target we evaluate, it achieves between 20% and 50% higher ASR and between 25% and 400% higher class-level coverage than recent state-of-the-art adaptive red teamers, while requiring no training. We release our code and the generated attacks to support reproducible, coverage-aware evaluation.

summary_es.tldr: AutoPI es un sistema que descubre nuevas formas de atacar a los LLM, yendo más allá de las vulnerabilidades conocidas.
summary_es.problema: Los sistemas de seguridad para LLM se evalúan con ataques conocidos, dejando vulnerabilidades nuevas sin descubrir y sin corregir.
summary_es.propuesta: AutoPI utiliza una taxonomía de ataques de 'prompt injection' para guiar la búsqueda de nuevas vulnerabilidades, adaptándose y generando ataques diversos.
summary_es.resultados: AutoPI logró cubrir todas las clases de ataques en un modelo (Qwen3.6-35B) y superó a otros sistemas en tasa de éxito y cobertura de ataques contra Claude Haiku 5.5.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite una evaluación de seguridad más completa y realista para los LLM, descubriendo debilidades que los métodos actuales pasan por alto.

papers.title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems
reasons: 🎯 temas: vuln & threats, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: One popular architecture for multi-agent systems (MAS) relies on an orchestrator that generates an initial plan, coordinates its execution, and dynamically revises the plan based on agent feedback when tasks cannot be fully specified in advance. This dynamic replanning introduces a critical vulnerability: malicious agents can embed instructions within their feedback to hijack the replanning process. Existing defenses focus exclusively on per-tool access control or static, pre-execution policy enforcement, leaving the replanning phase unsecured. We introduce Kaer, a multi-agent framework featuring security-aware replanning. Kaer shields the planner from untrusted agent feedback by conveying diagnostics to the replanning procedure strictly through abstract templates. Plan revisions are restricted to a set of deterministic repair operators, and all modified plans must satisfy preset policies. We create Cintra, a benchmark of simulated user tasks requiring replanning paired with adversarial objectives targeting the replanning phase. Using Cintra, we evaluate both task completion rates and system vulnerability to replanning exploits by malicious agents. Evaluating Kaer on Cintra against Magentic-One (an undefended MAS) and ControlValve (the state-of-the-art defense) demonstrates that Kaer achieves higher robustness than both systems while maintaining comparable utility to ControlValve. Although abstract failure templates slightly constrain utility on select tasks, Kaer enables MAS to perform secure, dynamic plan revisions without exposing the orchestrator to untrusted agent feedback.

summary_es.tldr: Kaer protege los sistemas multiagente de ataques maliciosos durante la reprogramación dinámica de planes.
summary_es.problema: Los sistemas multiagente (MAS) con reprogramación dinámica son vulnerables a que agentes maliciosos manipulen el proceso de revisión de planes a través de su feedback.
summary_es.propuesta: Kaer introduce una reprogramación consciente de la seguridad, utilizando plantillas abstractas para el feedback de los agentes y operadores de reparación deterministas para las revisiones de planes, asegurando que los planes modificados cumplan políticas preestablecidas.
summary_es.resultados: Kaer demuestra una mayor robustez contra exploits de reprogramación en comparación con Magentic-One y ControlValve, manteniendo una utilidad comparable a ControlValve en el benchmark Cintra. Las plantillas de fallo abstractas pueden limitar ligeramente la utilidad en tareas específicas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite que los sistemas multiagente realicen revisiones de planes dinámicas y seguras sin exponer el orquestador a feedback no confiable, crucial para aplicaciones críticas.

papers.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation
papers.abstract_en: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge. Existing goal-conditioned self-play frameworks rely primarily on static map-location goals and fail to reliably produce complex agent interactions such as aggressive tailgating or adversarial cut-offs. These agent interactions are necessary for rigorous autonomous vehicle (AV) testing. To address this, we present an extended multi-agent self-play framework that introduces agent-relative dynamic goals. By conditioning policies on this extended goal representation, our framework enables targeted, controllable scenario synthesis. We demonstrate that our approach successfully generates interactive driving behaviors that static-goal baselines cannot simulate, providing a flexible tool for long-tail scenario generation in AV testing.

summary_es.tldr: Genera escenarios de conducción autónoma complejos y controlables mediante auto-juego multi-agente con objetivos dinámicos.
summary_es.problema: Los métodos actuales de auto-juego multi-agente para generar escenarios de conducción autónoma no logran producir interacciones complejas y críticas para la seguridad, como adelantamientos agresivos o colas de tráfico, necesarios para pruebas rigurosas.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un marco de auto-juego multi-agente extendido que introduce objetivos dinámicos relativos al agente, permitiendo condicionar las políticas para la síntesis controlada de escenarios interactivos.
summary_es.resultados: El enfoque propuesto genera con éxito comportamientos de conducción interactivos que las líneas base con objetivos estáticos no pueden simular, facilitando la generación de escenarios de 'long-tail' para pruebas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite la creación de escenarios de prueba más realistas y controlables para vehículos autónomos, mejorando la seguridad y robustez al exponerlos a casos límite complejos y poco comunes.

papers.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
papers.abstract_en: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier. We propose Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), which uses binary safety labels to construct harmful and benign prototypes and makes predictions from relative prototype distances. JDPI uses only binary safety labels for encoder adaptation, prototype construction, and validation. In our setup, it uses fewer labeled examples than the classifier baseline (Method A) by avoiding the separate split used to train the downstream classifier. Across four benchmarks covering different input formats, contrastive fine-tuning improves JDPI's detection accuracy by 9.1-18.0 percentage points. Using the same encoder, JDPI achieves slightly higher ROC-AUC on one benchmark and stays within 0.017 of the baseline across all four. With dataset-specific adaptation, JDPI exceeds the released Llama Guard 3-8B baseline by 0.173-0.310 in ROC-AUC across the four benchmarks. In multi-turn replay on TomGibbs, JDPI uses accumulated user history as the conversation unfolds, achieving higher conversation-level accuracy than when it uses the current turn alone. Across 12 directed transfers, JDPI outperforms the classifier by an average of 1.59 percentage points in accuracy, demonstrating stronger cross-dataset robustness.

summary_es.tldr: Detecta 'jailbreaks' en modelos de lenguaje grandes usando prototipos de seguridad aprendidos, sin necesidad de clasificadores adicionales.
summary_es.problema: Los intentos de 'jailbreak' y los prompts dañinos dificultan el despliegue seguro de modelos de lenguaje grandes (LLMs).
summary_es.propuesta: Proponen Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), un método que utiliza representaciones aprendidas de forma contrastiva para detectar prompts maliciosos basándose en la distancia a prototipos de seguridad (dañinos vs. benignos), adaptando el modelo solo con etiquetas binarias.
summary_es.resultados: JDPI mejora la precisión de detección entre 9.1 y 18.0 puntos porcentuales en cuatro benchmarks. Supera a Llama Guard 3-8B en ROC-AUC (0.173-0.310) y muestra mayor robustez entre datasets (1.59 pp de mejora en precisión).
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite una detección de seguridad más eficiente y robusta en LLMs, reduciendo la necesidad de grandes conjuntos de datos etiquetados y mejorando la seguridad en aplicaciones prácticas.

papers.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
papers.abstract_en: Identifying high-impact attack paths in cyber-physical power systems is critical for improving grid resilience. Existing methods typically rely on either structural topology analysis or simulation-based cascading-failure models. Topology-based approaches capture connectivity but lack adversarial reasoning, while simulation-driven methods are primarily suited for offline analysis and are less effective for rapid evaluation of evolving attack scenarios. As a result, identifying realistic attack paths that jointly capture topology, threat semantics, and physical impact remains challenging. This paper presents a physics-grounded framework for identifying cyber-physical attack paths using large language models (LLMs), with cascading-failure-derived impact rankings used as physics-grounded references. The framework integrates system topology, LLM-guided STRIDE and MITRE ATT&CK threat modeling, and three baseline strategies for comparison: topology-driven, threat-driven, and fusion-based. Evaluation is performed using (i) critical-node overlap between LLM-inferred top-K rankings and cascading-failure-based ground truth; (ii) node-level similarity between LLM-inferred and reference paths; and (iii) path-level alignment capturing agreement in complete attack sequences. Results show that structured LLM-based threat modeling substantially improves alignment with physics-grounded references. In the cyber layer, critical-node overlap@3 increases from approximately 33% to as high as 100%, while node-level similarity reaches up to 65% and path-level alignment reaches up to 48%. In addition, the proposed framework reduces runtime by approximately 75--85% compared to the fusion-based baseline in the IEEE 14-bus system. These results suggest that LLM-guided attack path identification is a promising approach for efficient and impact-aware cyber-physical security analysis.

summary_es.tldr: Identifica rutas de ciberataques en redes eléctricas inteligentes usando LLMs, mejorando la eficiencia y la precisión.
summary_es.problema: Identificar rutas de ataque realistas en sistemas de energía ciberfísicos es difícil, ya que los métodos actuales no integran bien la topología, la semántica de amenazas y el impacto físico.
summary_es.propuesta: Un marco que utiliza LLMs para modelar amenazas (STRIDE, MITRE ATT&CK) y analizar la topología del sistema, guiado por rankings de impacto derivados de fallos en cascada.
summary_es.resultados: El solapamiento de nodos críticos mejora de ~33% a 100% (top-K). La similitud a nivel de nodo alcanza el 65% y la alineación a nivel de ruta el 48%. El tiempo de ejecución se reduce un 75-85% comparado con métodos de fusión.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite una identificación más rápida y precisa de las rutas de ataque más peligrosas en redes eléctricas, mejorando la resiliencia y la seguridad.

papers.title: When Shuffling Fails: Token Recovery from Obfuscated KV Caches
papers.abstract_en: LLM serving systems store, offload, and share KV caches, exposing token-level representations to infrastructure operators and co-tenants. Shuffled obfuscation combines secret linear transforms with fresh permutations, claiming security from b! possible shufflings. We show that input symmetry invalidates this counting argument: security depends on distinguishable outputs under chosen inputs. Repeated tokens produce identical first-layer Value rows, making every row permutation leave the data unchanged. Only auxiliary structures such as a single-row recovery marker vary, reducing the effective state space from b! to b. We construct Repeat-to-Reveal. The attacker collects the b distinguishable states from its own probes and exploits their rank-one differences to recover an equivalent denoiser without knowing the defender's secret parameters. A one-time calibration transfers across requests sharing the same secret epoch, enabling passive token-multiset recovery from subsequently observed cache blocks through public-model dictionary matching. We instantiate the attack on official KV-Cloak and evaluate 3,000 real WildChat user prompts across nine models and eleven configurations. The attack recovers the secret parameters with high accuracy and achieves 100 percent token-multiset recovery on GPU. Refreshing row-level secrets between epochs interrupts cross-request transfer, confirming secret reuse scope as the operative vulnerability. We further confirm orbit collapse on two other open-source defenses: the sequence-permutation implementation of Thomas et al. and PermLLM. The KV-Cloak developers invited a detailed report through their private vulnerability reporting channel.

summary_es.tldr: Se descubre una vulnerabilidad en la ofuscación de caché KV de LLM que permite recuperar tokens incluso con barajado de datos.
summary_es.problema: Los sistemas de servicio de LLM ofuscan las cachés KV (clave-valor) para proteger los tokens, pero la simetría de la entrada y los tokens repetidos invalidan los argumentos de seguridad de la ofuscación basada en permutaciones aleatorias.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone el ataque Repeat-to-Reveal, que explota las diferencias de rango uno entre estados distinguibles para recuperar un denoiser equivalente y, posteriormente, recuperar el multiconjunto de tokens de forma pasiva.
summary_es.resultados: El ataque recupera parámetros secretos con alta precisión y logra una recuperación del 100% de multiconjuntos de tokens en GPU. Se confirma la reutilización de secretos entre épocas como la vulnerabilidad operativa.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Esta vulnerabilidad expone la información sensible de los tokens en LLM, incluso con mecanismos de defensa, lo que requiere un rediseño de las estrategias de ofuscación para proteger la privacidad y la seguridad de los datos.

papers.title: Intent Contracts: Taking Tools Away from Agents
reasons: 🎯 temas: LLM, AI agents, adversarial ML
papers.abstract_en: Intent contracts are an authorization interface for tool-using LLM agents in which the planning model holds no tools. For each step it submits a short logged contract: a goal, a verbatim quotation of the user, and scope fields. Code validates the contract, and a small trusted model checks it against the user's words and writes the tool call itself. Provided the validation and dispatch code is correct, every executed call is written by the trusted model, the planner's influence on a call is confined to a contract logged before it, and the trusted side decides how much of a request to carry out. We compare contracts with two reviewers of planner-written commands: one sees only the user's words and the command, the information boundary of a reasoning-blind permission classifier, and one also sees the planner's goal and a checked quotation. With gpt-6.1-terra as planner and GLM-5.3-Flash as the trusted model on three AmPermBench task families, every object changed under contracts is named in the goal of the contract that produced the change; under review the planner names objects in its commands and rarely in its goals. When the planner adds work the user never asked for, contracts complete the user's task in 27/30 runs and the intent-visible reviewer in 16/30, because a reviewer can only refuse a whole command. Contracts do not reduce unauthorized actions. They are indistinguishable from blind review, and once the benchmark's environment terms are clarified, every condition that changes state hits a wrong target in 40-49% of those runs. That error is the planner's choice of objects for an ambiguous reference, which no trusted model here can see the environment to check; telling the executor to decline when unsure does not change it. We evaluate benign over-reach with one pair of models, not adversarial planners. We release the plugin and run records.

summary_es.tldr: Los contratos de intención limitan el acceso de los agentes LLM a las herramientas, mejorando la seguridad al separar la planificación de la ejecución.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes LLM que utilizan herramientas pueden ejecutar acciones no autorizadas o realizar trabajo adicional no solicitado por el usuario, lo que plantea riesgos de seguridad y eficiencia.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone un sistema de 'contratos de intención' donde el modelo de planificación no tiene acceso directo a las herramientas. En su lugar, genera un contrato con un objetivo, una cita textual del usuario y campos de alcance. Un modelo de confianza más pequeño valida este contrato y escribe la llamada a la herramienta.
summary_es.resultados: Bajo contratos de intención, cada objeto modificado se nombra en el objetivo del contrato. Los contratos completan tareas solicitadas por el usuario en 27/30 ejecuciones cuando el planificador añade trabajo extra, frente a 16/30 con un sistema de revisión. Sin embargo, los contratos no reducen las acciones no autorizadas y se observan errores del 40-49% en la selección de objetivos por referencia ambigua, ya que el modelo de confianza no puede verificar el entorno.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Este enfoque mejora la seguridad y el control sobre las acciones de los agentes LLM al limitar su acceso a herramientas y verificar explícitamente sus intenciones, aunque aún existen desafíos en la gestión de referencias ambiguas y acciones no autorizadas.

papers.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
papers.abstract_en: Autonomous LLM agents incur substantial cost and latency by invoking a large model (System-2) at every step, even when many intermediate actions choose among a small set of known candidates. Existing dual-system agents offload such decisions to a lightweight System-1 model, but rely on workflow-specific hooks authored per environment. We present AnyS1, a framework that turns human-authored procedural skills, whose instructions naturally specify where choices arise and which options apply, into a shared, domain-general source of decision points. Offline, AnyS1 mines grounded enumerable decisions across over 1,000 public skills, gathers execution-grounded trajectory states inside isolated containers to construct Any-DP, and trains a single calibrated 4B pointer System-1 with label smoothing. At run time, compiled workflows resolve routine decisions in one forward pass and fall back to System-2 when confidence falls below a calibrated threshold. Across three unseen benchmarks and distinct System-2 model families, AnyS1 preserves task reliability while cutting episode cost by 75-91% and model-call time by 63-92% relative to an uncompiled System-2 agent, and maintains performance under zero-shot threshold transfer.

summary_es.tldr: AnyS1 reduce drásticamente el costo y la latencia de los agentes IA al usar un modelo ligero para decisiones rutinarias, manteniendo la fiabilidad.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes IA autónomos son costosos y lentos porque usan modelos grandes (System-2) en cada paso, incluso para decisiones simples. Los sistemas actuales requieren adaptaciones específicas por entorno.
summary_es.propuesta: AnyS1 es un framework que convierte habilidades procedimentales humanas en puntos de decisión reutilizables. Mina decisiones de miles de habilidades, entrena un modelo ligero (System-1) y lo usa para resolver decisiones rutinarias, recurriendo al System-2 solo cuando es necesario.
summary_es.resultados: AnyS1 reduce el costo de episodios entre un 75-91% y el tiempo de llamadas al modelo entre un 63-92% en benchmarks no vistos, manteniendo la fiabilidad y el rendimiento bajo transferencia zero-shot.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite crear agentes IA más eficientes y económicos, haciéndolos más prácticos para aplicaciones del mundo real al optimizar el uso de recursos computacionales.

papers.title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
papers.abstract_en: Personalized vision-language assistants use visual observations and personal memories to provide advice tailored to the user. When the observed scene contains a physical hazard, personal context, such as allergies, medical conditions, or mobility constraints, can change what help is appropriate. Responding appropriately therefore requires recognizing the visible hazard and applying the relevant person's information. We introduce PReMind-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that evaluates this combination across diverse hazards and personal-memory conditions. It separately measures memory access, grounding, abstention, and hazard response, and assesses joint success on interdependency cases. Existing models often satisfy one requirement while failing the other, and training only for safety or personalization leaves a gap in joint success. We therefore propose PReMind, a two-phase reinforcement learning framework that combines on-demand and forced-call interactions (memory always retrieved) to jointly train grounded memory use and hazard response. At 4B, PReMind raises joint success from 12.9% to 28.6% over its base on the interdependency set and improves hazard adequacy and correct abstention on the main test. Joint-success gains persist under forced-call evaluation and under a second LLM judge across three Phase II seeds; averaged over these seeds, joint success also improves on unseen hazard groups. These findings highlight the need to evaluate and train personal assistants to connect visual evidence with the relevant person's context.

summary_es.tldr: Asistentes de IA personalizados necesitan entender peligros visuales y tu historial para darte consejos seguros y relevantes.
summary_es.problema: Los asistentes de IA personalizados fallan al combinar el reconocimiento de peligros visuales con el contexto personal del usuario (ej. alergias, condiciones médicas), lo que lleva a consejos inapropiados o inseguros.
summary_es.propuesta: Se propone PReMind, un marco de aprendizaje por refuerzo en dos fases que entrena conjuntamente el uso de memoria contextual y la respuesta a peligros, combinando interacciones bajo demanda y forzadas para mejorar la toma de decisiones.
summary_es.resultados: PReMind mejora el éxito conjunto (combinar peligro y contexto) del 12.9% al 28.6% en casos de interdependencia, y aumenta la adecuación de la respuesta al peligro y la abstención correcta en el conjunto de pruebas principal. Las mejoras persisten bajo diferentes evaluaciones y jueces.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Es crucial para desarrollar asistentes de IA más seguros y útiles que puedan adaptarse a las necesidades individuales, especialmente en situaciones que involucran riesgos físicos.

papers.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Video rough-cut is a core stage in media production workflows, organizing raw media materials into an initial video cut. Despite recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) for video-related tasks, automatic rough-cut remains underexplored, without a comprehensive benchmark for evaluation or mature workflows for producing executable cut plans. To address the evaluation gap, we introduce RoughCut-Bench, which covers two practical settings: (1) a visually driven setting over video cases, covering highlight detection and selection, source-video ordering, and adherence to user requirements when provided; and (2) a speech-driven setting over automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts, covering filler removal, expression deduplication, and low-value content trimming. Across these settings, the benchmark contains 101 visually driven cases, including 831 raw videos with 1,476 highlight annotations. It also includes 84 speech-driven cases, each consisting of an ASR transcript with annotated cleanup spans. The evaluation compares cut plans with these annotations in both settings and additionally uses a human-aligned agentic evaluator to assess rendered-cut quality in the visual setting. To apply LVLMs to automatic rough-cut, we further propose agentic workflows that guide them to produce structured cut plans from input materials. Experiments show that current LVLMs remain limited in producing expert-aligned cut plans. Our benchmark, code, and prompts are released at https://whalesong-zrs.github.io/RoughCut-Bench-Project-Page.

summary_es.tldr: Nuevo benchmark 'RoughCut-Bench' para evaluar modelos de lenguaje visual en la edición automática de video, revelando limitaciones actuales.
summary_es.problema: La edición automática de video, específicamente la fase de 'rough-cut' (primer corte), carece de benchmarks estandarizados y flujos de trabajo maduros para evaluar el rendimiento de los modelos de lenguaje visual (LVLMs).
summary_es.propuesta: Se introduce RoughCut-Bench, un benchmark con dos configuraciones (visual y basada en audio) y 101 casos de uso para evaluar LVLMs en tareas como detección de highlights, ordenación de clips y eliminación de contenido irrelevante. También se proponen flujos de trabajo 'agentic' para guiar a los LVLMs en la generación de planes de corte.
summary_es.resultados: Los experimentos demuestran que los LVLMs actuales tienen limitaciones significativas para generar planes de corte de calidad profesional. El benchmark incluye 831 videos y 84 transcripciones de audio con anotaciones específicas.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite medir y mejorar objetivamente la capacidad de los modelos de IA para automatizar tareas complejas de edición de video, acelerando flujos de trabajo en la producción multimedia.

papers.title: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
papers.abstract_en: NPU design-space exploration for LLM inference mainly relies on an expensive simulator that often returns only scalar feedback such as latency and power. Such feedback can rank evaluated configurations, but gives little information for deciding why a configuration is slow or which architecture parameter should be changed next. This limitation is especially severe because prefill and decode workloads can be limited by different resources, including compute throughput and HBM bandwidth. We propose CriticNPU, a sample-efficient DSE framework built around an online-calibrated mechanistic critic for NPU architecture design. The critic uses explicit hardware limits to evaluate NPU configurations: before simulation, it estimates whether a proposed configuration is likely to improve over the current best and filters weak candidates; after simulation, it aggregates operator-level runtimes into prefill/decode bottleneck summaries and predicts the effect of candidate parameter changes. We instantiate the critic with a Roofline-style model that derives compute and memory limits from architecture parameters and calibrates per-operator-type effective limits using simulator observations. And CriticNPU combines this critic with a workload extractor and an architecture planner to propose configurations. Across six LLM workloads and 16 deployment configurations per model, CriticNPU achieves best-or-tied-best latency in 74% of prefill and 87.5% of decode settings while using roughly half the simulator calls of competitive DSE baselines. We conduct extensive ablation studies and detailed analyses to validate the effectiveness of our method from multiple perspectives. Our code is available at https://github.com/bruno686/CriticNPU.

summary_es.tldr: Explora eficientemente el diseño de NPUs para LLMs, identificando cuellos de botella y mejorando el rendimiento con menos simulaciones.
summary_es.problema: La exploración del espacio de diseño de NPUs para inferencia de LLMs se basa en simuladores lentos que solo dan métricas generales (latencia, potencia), sin explicar por qué una configuración falla o cómo mejorarla, especialmente con cargas de trabajo mixtas (prefill/decode) limitadas por cómputo o ancho de banda de memoria.
summary_es.propuesta: Propone CriticNPU, un framework de exploración de diseño (DSE) eficiente en el uso de datos. Utiliza un 'crítico' mecanicista calibrado online que estima la viabilidad de configuraciones antes de la simulación y resume los cuellos de botella (cómputo/memoria) después de la simulación, basándose en límites explícitos de hardware y un modelo estilo Roofline.
summary_es.resultados: CriticNPU logra el mejor o igual mejor latencia en el 74% de los casos de prefill y el 87.5% de los casos de decode, utilizando aproximadamente la mitad de las llamadas al simulador comparado con métodos de base competitivos.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite diseñar NPUs más eficientes para LLMs de forma más rápida y con mejor comprensión de los factores de rendimiento, reduciendo costos computacionales y acelerando la optimización de hardware para IA.

papers.title: StatePortal: Agentic Checkpoint Synthesis for Testing Deep States in Interactive Software
papers.abstract_en: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines do not expose. We introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes a checkpoint, an artifact that restores that state and can be versioned and replayed, from a natural-language functional test case and read-only access to the target's source code. The checkpoint is restored through a per-application hook that an onboarding agent binds or synthesizes once without hand-written hook code. Because a checkpoint can satisfy state checks while rendering incorrectly, checkpoints are scored by hybrid programmatic-state and visual evaluation: acceptance requires both a programmatic-state oracle and a visual oracle to pass. We calibrate the visual oracle against a blinded cross-VLM reference. We release DeepStateBench, 61 deep-state tasks across 10 interactive applications that span five language families and six rendering stacks, with source sizes from 874 to 7.2M lines. Across three registered models, a GUI agent seeded with synthesized checkpoints completes 10.4% of trials, compared with 0% without seeding under the same pixel action space, while StatePortal, which also delivers the target action through the hook, completes 27.5%. Over 1,361 replays of 112 checkpoints, 98.90% reproduce the original verdict with zero model calls, and the hybrid oracle detects 96.25% (77/80) of controlled visual faults invisible to programmatic-state checks alone. We open-source our code at https://github.com/pzy2000/State_Portal and website at https://stateportal.mineyosemite.chatgpt.site

summary_es.tldr: StatePortal automatiza la creación de puntos de control para probar estados complejos en software interactivo, mejorando drásticamente la eficiencia de las pruebas.
summary_es.problema: Probar software interactivo con interfaces gráficas (GUI) es costoso, especialmente para alcanzar 'estados profundos' que requieren largas secuencias de interacciones. La automatización actual falla porque no puede acceder a los árboles de renderizado interno y el costo de alcanzar estos estados se repite con cada cambio de código.
summary_es.propuesta: StatePortal es un agente que genera 'puntos de control' (artefactos que restauran un estado específico) a partir de descripciones en lenguaje natural y acceso al código fuente. Utiliza un hook de aplicación para restaurar el estado y evalúa la corrección mediante una combinación de verificación programática y visual.
summary_es.resultados: Los agentes guiados por puntos de control de StatePortal completaron el 10.4% de las pruebas (frente al 0% sin ellos). StatePortal, que también usa el hook para la acción, alcanzó el 27.5%. El 98.90% de los puntos de control reproducen veredictos sin llamadas a modelos, y el sistema de oráculo híbrido detecta el 96.25% de fallos visuales.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Reduce significativamente el esfuerzo y el costo de probar software interactivo complejo, permitiendo una detección más temprana y eficiente de errores, especialmente aquellos relacionados con la interfaz visual y estados profundos.
